patterns.text: Bash is the noisiest tool every week, with error rates far above read.
Advisor-doctrine sessions land in the top-5 costliest sessions of the week in 4 of 5 weeks.
Edit tool error rate (main) jumped sharply in the back half of the month.
Eval tool error rate climbed steadily across the month.
The tofu project family's share of weekly prompts fell every week.
Weekly cost swung sharply in both directions rather than trending.

month_over_month: Weekly cost swung both directions in September (-54%, +39%, -48%, -36%) instead of August's steady weekly fall.
Tofu's prompt share reversed from August's climb (74% to 91%) to a September slide (84% to 22%).
Opus's August dominance (62-71% of spend every week) broke in week one: gpt-5.6-sol took 59.5% of spend ($907.38 of $1525.34) while opus held only 38.1% ($581.61).
Advisor-doctrine top-5 placement held steady: 4 of 4 weeks in August, 4 of 5 weeks in September.
questions: Weekly digests for 2026-09-25 and 2026-09-28 overlap by about 4.7 days (09-21 07:02 to 09-26 00:00), double-counting sessions such as worktree-silver-stone-bb37's $34.47 advisor.doctrine run in both weeks' totals. Does the September rollup need de-duplication?
What changed in the edit pipeline between 09-18 and 09-25 to push its error rate from under 1% to 5.9% and then 7.8%?
Why did gpt-5.6-sol cost more than opus in week one ($907.38 vs $581.61) after being the cheap, high-volume model through all of August?
